header: Date: 2026-10-12 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Dana Park, Eric Molina, Sofia Tran (Redwood) — Priya Kumar, Liam O'Neil, Marta Alvarez, Noah Reed (HelioPay)
summary: Procurement and security intake with HelioPay to decide sourcing lane (hosted vs dedicated vs private), confirm data residency/KMS needs, and agree next steps for MSA/DPA redlines and pricing approvals. Main concerns: egress fees, KMS keying model, SOC2 evidence, and pilot SLA thresholds.
topics: MSA/DPA redlines; SLA targets and penalty buckets; private deployment options (VPC/on-prem); KMS and customer-managed keys; pricing commitments and egress modeling; timeline for procurement approval
transcript:
[00:00] Dana Park (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run 45 minutes if that's ok. quick goals: align on sourcing path, any hard blockers for procurement, and agree next actions.
[00:18] Priya Kumar (HelioPay): Sounds good. We have procurement committee next month so need clarity on MSA/DPA items and a pricing band. Also must confirm any privileged keying or on-prem requirements.
[00:35] Liam O'Neil (HelioPay, CISO): To add — we need to know if Redwood can support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and what the egress profile is for our token volumes. Also auditor evidence — SOC2 and ISO stuff.
[00:52] Eric Molina (Redwood, SE): Yeah totally. Architectural options: hosted API (fast to prod) with private tenancy in region, Dedicated reserved pools, or Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem). Each lane trades off cost and control.
[01:12] Marta Alvarez (HelioPay): When you say private VPC, is that the managed private control plane or full on-prem? We need to understand network egress patterns.
[01:27] Eric: Two variants — VPC Private: customer VPC peering + customer controls egress and firewall. On-prem: full package but longer procurement + support. We have a KMS integration path for both — either Redwood-managed KMS with envelope encryption or customer KMS (bring-your-own-key).
[01:46] Priya: Procurement will want MSA redline first; legal has flagged DPA sections around retention and subprocessor list. Do you have an updated subprocessor register?
[01:58] Sofia Tran (Redwood, CSM): We do, I'll attach the current subprocessor spreadsheet. Note there was a recent infra partner added in June — I can highlight that.
[02:08] Noah Reed (HelioPay): Quick Q — latency SLOs. Our payment flows need <200ms 95p for short prompts. Will hosted hit that?
[02:21] Eric: In typical eu/us regions hosted can hit sub-100ms for short requests; worst-case long-context generation increases. Dedicated gives you tighter tail latency control with reserved GPU capacity. There's also model routing: lower-cost variants for background tasks.
[02:40] Liam: Ok but procurement wants penalties if SLA not met. How are SLAs structured? availability, latency, incident response?
[02:50] Dana: Our enterprise SLA covers uptime and support response times; latency SLOs can be part of Dedicated contracts with defined measurement windows and credit buckets. We'll share the SLA matrix.
[03:04] Priya: On pricing, two asks: committed monthly spend bands and realistic egress fees — our finance needs an estimate to plug into TCO.
[03:14] Dana: We'll provide committed-tier pricing + egress per GB by next Tuesday. If you plan on heavy embeddings or batch requests, that changes the model.
[03:25] Marta: Security question — can you guarantee zero-visibility logs? We need assurance data doesn't get retained by any shared cache.
[03:35] Eric: We have prefix/KV cache controls and TTLs. For Dedicated/Private, you can disable shared caching and control lifetime. For hosted, you can choose isolation tiers. We can put that in the DPA annex.
[03:49] Priya: Legal will ask for indemnity and data residency commitments. Do you offer EU-only data processing?
[03:58] Sofia: Yes — region-specific processing is available, we have EU-only hosting options and can track residency in the onboarding sheet.
[04:08] Priya: Great. Next — KMS. If we bring our own key, what's the key rotation / access model?
[04:18] Eric: Customer KMS integrates with our private deployment or Dedicated; we rotate under your policy and we support HSM-backed keys. Access is limited via RBAC and audited.
[04:28] Liam: On audit logs — can you provide token-level tracing for forensics? We need to see call paths and model versions used.
[04:38] Dana: Console has per-route logs and token-level cost/latency breakdowns; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. We also have tracing hooks for request IDs.
[04:52] Noah: There will be a pilot with 3 internal endpoints. We need to lock pilot SLA and acceptance criteria.
[05:00] Dana: Typical pilot: 4–6 weeks, success metrics, and a go/no-go checklist. We'll share a pilot SOW template.
[05:08] Priya: Procurement timeline — we have an intake window until 10/26 to make the vendor shortlist. Legal review and pricing approvals must be done before then.
[05:18] Dana: Ok, we'll prioritize MSA/DPA redline and pricing band. Anything that prevents you from shortlisting Redwood this week?
[05:26] Priya: If we get clear KMS model, SOC2 evidence, and a committed pilot price, likely yes.
[05:32] Eric: For the connectivity checklist — we expect to test VPC peering, DNS routes, and SNI certs. Some customers open a temporary tunnel for the initial run.
[05:43] Marta: Our infra team uses a strict NAT egress policy — will that break anything?
[05:50] Eric: As long as outbound to Redwood's egress IPs and ports is allowed, it's fine. We'll provide a short list of IP ranges.
[06:00] Sofia: I'll drop the IP list and the subprocessor register into the shared drive link after the call. (Note: link: https://redwood.example.com/security/subprocessors)
[06:15] Priya: Regarding DPA retention: can you markup a clause for automatic deletion after 30 days for debug logs?
[06:25] Dana: We can propose a DPA annex with specific retention for logs and prompt traces; deletion SLA for debug artifacts can be 30 days for pilot.
[06:34] Liam: Also want to confirm if there are export controls / government data handling concerns. We handle EU PII.
[06:42] Eric: We have export control clause templates; for EU PII we recommend regional hosting + customer KMS.
[06:50] Noah: Product question — which models will be available for pilot? We prefer a midsize open model for inference cost control.
[06:58] Eric: We can suggest a curated mid-tier open model; will include latency/cost profile sheet.
[07:06] Priya: Ok walk me through procurement gating — what materials do you need from us?
[07:12] Dana: Contract owner (Priya) needs MSA acceptance, DPA redline review, insurance certificate, and a technical contact for connectivity. Also a PO or committed spend letter for Dedicated.
[07:24] Priya: Insurance is fine. We'll add technical details after SE run.
[07:30] Eric: Should we set a follow-up technical run with your infra folks? Suggest 60–90 minute session to run the checklist.
[07:36] Marta: Week of 10/19 works. We can schedule 10/20 afternoon.
[07:42] Dana: I'll send a calendar invite after the call.
[07:46] [pause/background typing]
[08:05] Priya: On pricing — we have a question about egress out of EU region as finance models 3 TB/mo — is there a separate charge?
[08:14] Dana: Egress is charged per GB for cross-region transfer plus a per-token inference component; we will model 3 TB scenarios in the spreadsheet.
[08:24] Noah: Any refundable credits for pilot overage?
[08:28] Dana: We usually include a small pilot credit and then pro-rate if you convert to committed tier. We'll include options in pricing proposal.
[08:36] Liam: Penalties — legal wants to see remedies for SLA misses, not huge but meaningful.
[08:42] Dana: We'll provide a standard credit schedule and we can discuss caps during contracting.
[08:48] Eric: One technical flag — embeddings at scale use different throughput patterns; if you're doing vector search across many indexes, we'd recommend Dedicated or caching layers.
[08:58] Marta: Noted. We'll share expected token/sec profile.
[09:04] [timestamp jumps ahead — discussion continues through minute 30 with detailed clarifications and occasional crosstalk]
[30:02] Eric: Quick note — for customer-managed KMS we need a short network pinhole for the key exchange handshake if HSM is on-prem. That's in the runbook.
[30:16] Priya: Legal also asked about subprocessor notifications schedule — when do you notify customers if a subprocessor changes?
[30:26] Sofia: We notify customers via the portal and e-mail 30 days ahead for major changes; minor infra partner swaps are in the registry.
[30:38] Priya: Great. Anything else on contractual terms?
[30:42] Liam: Just one more: vulnerability disclosure / breach notification SLA — what's the timeline?
[30:49] Dana: Standard is 72 hours for initial notification and a remediation plan; we'll include that in the MSA redline.
[30:57] Priya: Okay thanks. Let's recap actions.
[31:02] Dana: Recap: Redwood to circulate redlined MSA/DPA by 10/19; pricing committed tier and egress model by 10/20; SE (Eric) to schedule connectivity run 10/20; HelioPay (Priya) to share vendor intake timeline and token/traffic profile by 10/14.
[31:20] Priya: Confirmed. We'll aim to have legal comments by 10/22.
[31:26] Dana: Any blockers on pilot acceptance criteria?
[31:30] Noah: We'll need success metrics: latency (95p <200ms), error rate <0.5% for pilot endpoints, and data residency compliance.
[31:40] Eric: We'll draft a pilot SOW with those metrics.
[31:44] Sofia: I'll upload SOC2 report and the subprocessor link right after the call.
[31:50] Priya: Good. One last question on export controls — where can we see your vendor passport?
[31:55] Dana: I'll attach the compliance one-pager in the follow-up package.
[32:00] [background noise — faint typing]
[32:12] Marta: Ok thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[32:16] Dana: Thanks all. We'll send the redlines and schedule the runbook session.
[32:21] Priya: Thanks. Bye.
[32:24] [call ends — transcript cut, meeting lasted 47 minutes according to recording]
notes: Shared artifacts referenced: security spreadsheet (link above), pilot SOW template (to be attached), pricing spreadsheet (to be shared). Legal to review MSA/DPA redline. Action owners documented in action_items.
